successors.note: 29 June 1880: Pōmare V gave Tahiti and its dependencies to France (Kingdom of Tahiti page). The French protectorate over the kingdom began on 9 September 1842.

capitals.name: Pare (Porionuʻu), Tahiti
capitals.note: Pōmare I was ariʻi-rahi of Porionuʻu and born at Pare; Pōmare II was installed at Tarahoi (13 February 1791) and baptised at the Royal Chapel, Papeʻete (16 May 1819). Coordinates approximate; no page opened gives them.

rulers.name: Pōmare I
rulers.note: Reign 1788 to 13 February 1791 (infobox); abdicated 1791 but remained regent for Pōmare II until 1803; died 3 September 1803.

rulers.name: Pōmare II
rulers.note: Installed at Tarahoi 13 February 1791; the Kingdom page's lead also says 1803-1821 and 1782-1821; died 7 December 1821 at Motu Uta, Papeete.

rulers.name: Pōmare III
rulers.note: Born 25 June 1820, crowned 21 April 1824, reigned under a council of regency until his death on 8 January 1827.

rulers.name: Pōmare IV
rulers.note: 11 January 1827 to 17 September 1877; under French administration from 1843 (Kingdom page) or 1847 (Pōmare IV page).

rulers.name: Pōmare V
rulers.note: King from 17 September 1877, crowned 24 September 1877; gave Tahiti to France 29 June 1880.

correction.text: the islands of Tahiti itself, Moʻorea, Mehetiʻa, and the Tetiʻaroa group (Pōmare I page); the gazetteer's Tahiti region is the Papeete-Moʻorea cells

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Tahiti row). 'He thus became the first king of unified Tahiti in 1788'; the kingdom was 'composed of the islands of Tahiti itself, Moʻorea, Mehetiʻa, and the Tetiʻaroa group' (undated). The Leeward Islands (Raiatea, Huahine, Bora Bora) are not included: the Leewards War page says Pōmare II held only 'nominal suzerainty' over them and the 1847 Jarnac Convention recognised their independence. No page gives an area. At the grid's resolution the two small atolls fall out and the keyframe is the Tahiti-Moʻorea cells (about 1,260 km2). 1808-1815 (ledger /1 and /2): Tahiti island itself was lost to the rebel chiefs from 22 December 1808 ('forced to take refuge in Moʻorea') until the Battle of Te Feʻi Pī on 12 November 1815 (Kingdom of Tahiti page), leaving the king Moʻorea; the keyframe keeps the full shape and the ledger loss and gain carry the change (note added by reviewer oc-01).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the same islands as a French protectorate (infobox 'French protectorate (1842-1880)'; 'Tahiti and Moorea continued to be ruled under the French protectorate', Franco-Tahitian War page). The ledger and the war carry the 1844-1846 contest; the suzerain (the French dossier) should draw the tint.

region.text: the islands of Tahiti itself, Moʻorea, Mehetiʻa, and the Tetiʻaroa group (Pōmare I page); the gazetteer's Tahiti region is the Papeete-Moʻorea cells

ledger.note: 1788: Pōmare I becomes the first king of unified Tahiti. 'He thus became the first king of unified Tahiti in 1788'; the infobox of the Kingdom page reads 'Founded by Pōmare I: 1788/91'. The land (Tahiti, Moʻorea, Mehetiʻa, Tetiʻaroa) is named by the page without a date, so the region is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Tahiti, from which Pōmare II was driven to Eimeo (Moʻorea)

ledger.note: 1808: rebels drive Pōmare II from Tahiti to Moʻorea. 'in 1808 they drove him from Tahiti to the nearby island of Eimeo'; 'he was subsequently forced to take refuge in Moʻorea 22 December 1808'. The page does not say how much of Tahiti the rebels held; Moʻorea stays with the king. Fix fx-40 (2 Nov 2026), window request R113: the region named the place 'Moorea', unknown to the gazetteer, so the event was skipped; it is now the disk lon -149.83, lat -17.53, 15 km (Moʻorea). The Moorea page (opened 2 Nov 2026) gives no coordinates, only 'lying 17 kilometres (11 mi) northwest of Tahiti' and 'about 16 km across'; the disk is the window's centre, and it holds exactly the one land cell (17.46 S, 149.83 W) of the gazetteer's Tahiti region that lies west-north-west of Papeete, so 'Tahiti minus Moʻorea' leaves the four cells of Tahiti island. Pōmare II page (opened 2 Nov 2026): 'he was subsequently forced from Tahiti and took refuge in Moʻorea on 22 December 1808'; 'returned and defeated his enemies at the Battle of Te Feipī, on 11 November 1815' (a footnote: the missionaries recorded Sunday 12 November 1815); 'recognised as undisputed king ... of Tahiti, Moʻorea and its dependencies'. The page does not say who held Moʻorea in between.

region.text: Tahiti, retaken from the rebel chiefs

ledger.note: 1815: Pōmare II wins Tahiti back at Te Feipī. 'with Pomare winning the decisive Battle of Te Fe'i Pī, on 12 November 1815'. The page names the battle and date, not the land regained. Fix fx-40 (2 Nov 2026), R113: the place 'Moorea' is replaced by the disk lon -149.83, lat -17.53, 15 km (see ledger/1).

region.text: the island of Tahiti, fought over from March 1844

ledger.note: 1844: Tahitians rise against the French. 'began an armed resistance on 13 March 1844'; the first battle on the page is Mahaena, 17 April 1844. The French held the coast around Papeete after the November 1843 annexation ('Dupetit Thouars deposed the queen ... and formally annexed the islands'); the Kingdom of Tahiti page dates the war 1843-1847, this page 1844-1847.

1846: the last Tahitian stronghold falls. 'the capture of Fort Fautaua on 17 December 1846', after 'the defeat of the Tahitians at the Battle of Punaruu in May 1846'. The page gives no treaty; Pōmare IV returned from exile in February 1847 and accepted the protectorate.
1847: the seat is Papeete. Infobox 'Capital: Papeete (from 1847)'; the page gives no earlier capital, so the Pare seat before 1847 is the researcher's reading of the Pōmare I and II pages.

region.text: the islands of Tahiti itself, Moʻorea, Mehetiʻa, and the Tetiʻaroa group (Pōmare I page); the gazetteer's Tahiti region is the Papeete-Moʻorea cells

ledger.note: 1880: Pōmare V gives Tahiti and its dependencies to France. 'On 29 June 1880, he gave Tahiti and its dependencies to France'; infobox 'Annexation by France and dissolution: 29 June 1880'.

wars.name: Franco-Tahitian War
wars.outcome: French victory: Fort Fautaua fell on 17 December 1846 and Queen Pōmare IV returned from exile in February 1847 to rule under the protectorate; the Anglo-French Convention of 1847 recognised the independence of Huahine, Raiatea and Bora Bora.
wars.note: The Kingdom of Tahiti and Pōmare IV pages date the war 1843-1847; the war page, 1844-1847 with armed resistance from 13 March 1844. Mahaena 17 April 1844; Punaruu May 1846.

wars.name: Tahitian civil war and Battle of Te Feipī

zones.text: Tahiti, from which Pōmare II was driven in 1808

wars.outcome: Pōmare II, who had taken refuge in Moʻorea on 22 December 1808, won the decisive Battle of Te Feipī on 12 November 1815 and was baptised on 16 May 1819.
wars.note: The page names no rebel leader; the fighting between December 1808 and November 1815 is not dated on the page. Fix fx-40: the zone's place 'Moorea' replaced by a lon/lat disk (see ledger/1).

certainty.note: Island coasts are exact; what is soft is the extent of Pōmare authority (Tetiʻaroa, Mehetiʻa, the Tuamotus, the nominal suzerainty over the Leeward Islands).
Protectorate of France; the islands are the same, the Leeward kingdoms stay outside until 1888-1897.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks (no Tahiti or French Polynesia row before the modern country). The French protectorate (9 September 1842 per the infobox) and the November 1843 annexation are France's relation to this kingdom: bourbon-kingdom-of-france (to 1847), french-second-republic, second-french-empire and french-third-republic should carry vassal_start 1842 / vassal_end 1880 with counterpart kingdom-of-tahiti (report: problems). The Leeward Islands kingdoms (Raiatea and Tahaa, Huahine, Bora Bora) were independent of Tahiti under the 1847 Jarnac Convention until their 1888-1897 annexation (Leewards War page: Huahine 16 March 1888, Raiatea 17 March 1888, Bora Bora 19 March 1888; Huahine ceded 11 September 1895; Bora Bora abdicated 21 September 1895; Chamber ratified annexation 19 November 1897) and need dossiers (counterparts_needing_dossiers); the Kingdom of Tahiti page says Pōmare IV 'reunited' Raiatea and Porapora with Tahiti but gives no date, so they are not drawn as Tahitian. Not on any page opened: Tahiti Iti/Taiarapu and the Papara and Vehiatua rivalries before 1788; the dates of the Tuamotu and Mehetiʻa/Tetiʻaroa accessions; a Wikidata id. Pōmare II's start is dated three ways on the Kingdom page (1782, 1791, 1803); this dossier follows 13 February 1791. The Pritchard affair and the 1842 treaty are not dated by the Franco-Tahitian War page (only 'between 1838 and 1842'). Region names: the gazetteer has 'Tahiti' (Papeete 60 km) but no place 'Moorea' (used for the loss/gain subtraction, centre about -149.83, -17.54): gazetteer_names_needed. Coordinates of Pare are approximate. [Fix fx-40, 2 Nov 2026, R113] 'Moorea' (not in the gazetteer) replaced by the disk lon -149.83, lat -17.53, 15 km in ledger/1, ledger/2 and the civil-war zone; the gazetteer names needed: place Moorea / Moʻorea / Eimeo.
